rationale: This benchmark is a single small, loop-hot bubblesort kernel with no source-level profile detail available, so the table favors passes that are cheap, correct, and effective on tight arithmetic/comparison code while restraining those whose overhead scales with execution count. SUB and BCF get the highest SecurityGain/DiversityGain weights because instruction substitution and bogus control flow obscure the swap/compare core at near-zero correctness risk and modest cost on a tiny function; FLA is weighted strongly since flattening the nested loop structure defeats static control-flow recovery, but its RuntimeCost weight is kept moderate because the sort's inner loop is executed O(n^2) times. IBR is a mid-weight secondary diversifier (indirect branching hinders dynamic analysis) with a slightly elevated runtime weight for the same hot-loop reason. SPLIT adds little on a function this small, and ICALL/IGV target indirect calls and global-variable accesses that a self-contained sort barely exercises, so all three are weighted low enough that the selector will effectively skip them, keeping size and runtime overhead concentrated where it buys real resistance.
